cards.front: Complete the rule: No manual alone teaches driving skill; safe operation.
cards.back: No manual alone teaches driving skill; safe operation comes only through instruction, practice and applied choices.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Distraction means eyes off the road, hands off.
cards.back: Distraction means eyes off the road, hands off the wheel or mind off driving, while ninety percent of decisions rest on vision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Crash risk rises with any side task or.
cards.back: Crash risk rises with any side task or glance away, spanning texting, phones, food, passengers, grooming, reading, navigation, video, audio controls and fatigue.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Texting is the worst distraction because it.
cards.back: Texting is the worst distraction because it combines manual, visual and cognitive load at once.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A text costs five seconds of eyes-off-road, which.
cards.back: A text costs five seconds of eyes-off-road, which the handbook likens to crossing a football field blindfolded at fifty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: So-called multitasking is rapid single-task switching, and every.
cards.back: So-called multitasking is rapid single-task switching, and every distraction raises crash risk for all road users.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never text or call while driving, speak up.
cards.back: Never text or call while driving, speak up as a passenger, and urge phone-free driving on others.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Most Montana cities ban texting and phoning while.
cards.back: Most Montana cities ban texting and phoning while driving; handle needs only after pulling over and stopping.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep eyes on the road, hands on the.
cards.back: Keep eyes on the road, hands on the wheel, everyone buckled, and alcohol out of driving.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Texting combines manual, visual and cognitive load, while.
cards.back: Texting combines manual, visual and cognitive load, while other distractions typically load fewer channels at once.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Start per the owner manual with the brake.
cards.back: Start per the owner manual with the brake set, manuals out of gear with clutch as needed, and automatics in park.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Accelerate gently since hard starts spin wheels and.
cards.back: Accelerate gently since hard starts spin wheels and slide the car, and shift manuals without over-revving or stalling.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Grip opposite sides of the wheel, such as.
cards.back: Grip opposite sides of the wheel, such as nine-and-three or eight-and-four with wheel-mounted airbags, for comfort and control.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Look far down the road to anticipate.
cards.back: Look far down the road to anticipate steering needs in time for smooth, safe moves.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Corner with hand-over-hand grip and straighten by hand.
cards.back: Corner with hand-over-hand grip and straighten by hand, never palming one-handed or letting the wheel slip.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Automatic starts need park and manuals need neutral.
cards.back: Automatic starts need park and manuals need neutral with clutch as required, with the brake set in both cases.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Watch the speedometer since drivers misjudge speed.
cards.back: Watch the speedometer since drivers misjudge speed, especially leaving fast roads for slow local streets.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Follow posted limits for safety and drive below.
cards.back: Follow posted limits for safety and drive below them on bad roads or weather; standard limits sit in the driving-rules chapter.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Anticipate stops early because sudden braking risks.
cards.back: Anticipate stops early because sudden braking risks skids, lost control and rear-end hits from behind.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Ease off or change lanes early to avoid.
cards.back: Ease off or change lanes early to avoid stopping at all, or at least to stop gradually and safely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Most driving depends on vision, and missed sights.
cards.back: Most driving depends on vision, and missed sights top crash causes, so scan ahead, sides and behind with headlights in poor light.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never look away more than a few seconds.
cards.back: Never look away more than a few seconds; pull over to read maps or handle anything demanding eyes.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoid phone and radio use in motion even.
cards.back: Avoid phone and radio use in motion even hands-free, and never drive wearing headphones or earbuds that block horns and sirens.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Pass roadside incidents without staring or slowing to.
cards.back: Pass roadside incidents without staring or slowing to gawk, keeping eyes ahead and clearing the scene promptly and safely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Scan ahead, to the sides and behind to.
cards.back: Scan ahead, to the sides and behind to spot problems, road users, warning signs and direction signs early.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Look at least ten seconds ahead to brake.
cards.back: Look at least ten seconds ahead to brake and steer early, saving fuel, smoothing traffic and holding a straighter line.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Ten seconds spans about one city block in.
cards.back: Ten seconds spans about one city block in town and about four blocks or a quarter mile on highways.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Search the sides constantly since crossings can.
cards.back: Search the sides constantly since crossings can appear anywhere, especially at intersections and railroad tracks.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Intersections include any merging or crossing point; look.
cards.back: Intersections include any merging or crossing point; look left, right and across before entering or starting.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Left across oncoming traffic needs a safe gap.
cards.back: Left across oncoming traffic needs a safe gap, a clear destination street, and one last oncoming check; one-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Right turns need clear left and no conflicting.
cards.back: Right turns need clear left and no conflicting oncoming lefts, plus a pedestrian check; right on red is allowed unless barred.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never trust signals to stop cross traffic.
cards.back: Never trust signals to stop cross traffic; watch for red-light runners, especially just after green.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Edge forward slowly when views are blocked so.
cards.back: Edge forward slowly when views are blocked so crossing drivers see the car nose and can warn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Scan sides near shops, lots, work zones, sidewalks.
cards.back: Scan sides near shops, lots, work zones, sidewalks, playgrounds and school yards where entries are likely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Look up and down every rail crossing without.
cards.back: Look up and down every rail crossing without assuming no train; at multi-track crossings wait until the passed train clears in case another hides behind it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check behind often, especially in heavy traffic and.
cards.back: Check behind often, especially in heavy traffic and before lane changes, slowdowns, backing or long downhill runs.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Lane changes, merges and curb entries all require.
cards.back: Lane changes, merges and curb entries all require confirming the target lane is empty beside and behind.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal the lane change, clear mirrors for occupants.
cards.back: Signal the lane change, clear mirrors for occupants and passers, then check the blind spot over the shoulder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Glance quickly without leaving the road ahead, rechecking.
cards.back: Glance quickly without leaving the road ahead, rechecking mirrors and the blind spot just before moving.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check the far lane for converging drivers and.
cards.back: Check the far lane for converging drivers and watch for hard-to-see bikes, motorcycles and pedestrians, especially entering from curbs or driveways.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check behind on every slowdown, particularly sudden.
cards.back: Check behind on every slowdown, particularly sudden ones or where followers least expect braking.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Leave the curb with a signal.
cards.back: Leave the curb with a signal, a left-shoulder look, and a safe gap.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Time the gap by counting thousand-seconds to a.
cards.back: Time the gap by counting thousand-seconds to a fixed object; the count equals seconds of looking ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Early moves give followers more reaction time.
cards.back: Early moves give followers more reaction time, keeping traffic steady and safer for everyone behind.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Speedometers correct misjudged speed, while posted limits.
cards.back: Speedometers correct misjudged speed, while posted limits set the ceiling that bad conditions lower.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A plain green never excuses skipping the left-right.
cards.back: A plain green never excuses skipping the left-right check, since cross traffic may run its red.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Mirrors clear the lanes beside and behind, while.
cards.back: Mirrors clear the lanes beside and behind, while only an over-shoulder look clears the blind spot.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A city ten-seconds means watching one block ahead.
cards.back: A city ten-seconds means watching one block ahead, while a highway ten-seconds means four blocks or a quarter mile.

cards.front: Complete the rule: One-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred.
cards.back: One-way to one-way lefts are allowed unless barred, while lefts across oncoming traffic need a safe gap and clear exit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Hands-free calling still steals attention like hand-held.
cards.back: Hands-free calling still steals attention like hand-held use, while headphones additionally block emergency sound.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Night vision falls while ninety percent of decisions.
cards.back: Night vision falls while ninety percent of decisions still need sight, so slow down for road, car and weather conditions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Burn headlights from a half hour after sunset.
cards.back: Burn headlights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, or whenever people and vehicles vanish inside five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Upper beams must reveal people and vehicles three.
cards.back: Upper beams must reveal people and vehicles three hundred fifty feet out and lower beams one hundred feet; dim within one thousand feet of oncoming traffic and five hundred behind followed vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Meet night traffic by watching the right road.
cards.back: Meet night traffic by watching the right road edge instead of the beams, and check the dimmer when flashed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Back up as little as possible, favoring drive-through.
cards.back: Back up as little as possible, favoring drive-through spaces; check behind before entering since children and small objects hide from the seat.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reverse slowly while looking through the rear window.
cards.back: Reverse slowly while looking through the rear window with an arm over the seatback, never trusting mirrors alone, and use a guide outside when possible.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Never drive on parking lights alone, and douse.
cards.back: Never drive on parking lights alone, and douse spotlights for approaching vehicles; at dusk or overcast, switch headlights on.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Tinted and photo-gray lenses can steal up to.
cards.back: Tinted and photo-gray lenses can steal up to thirty percent of night vision, so treat them with caution after dark.

cards.front: Complete the rule: With breakdowns or tire failure, slow gently, regain.
cards.back: With breakdowns or tire failure, slow gently, regain control before leaving the lane, then pull as far right as safely possible with parking lights on and headlights dimmed at night.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Limit long night drives, breaking at least every.
cards.back: Limit long night drives, breaking at least every two hours for air and alertness, and nap or lodge when drowsy rather than pressing on.
